fullDescription: Join us for some fun by talking about Speak Up! by Rebecca Burgess! The first 4 students to register will receive a free copy of the graphic novel. About Speak Up! : Twelve-year-old Mia is just trying to navigate a world that doesn't understand her true autistic self. While she wishes she could stand up to her bullies, she's always been able to express her feelings through singing and songwriting, even more so with her best friend, Charlie, who is nonbinary, putting together the best beats for her. Together, they've taken the internet by storm; little do Mia's classmates know that she's the viral singer Elle-Q! But while the chance to perform live for a local talent show has Charlie excited, Mia isn't so sure. She'll have to decide whether she'll let her worries about what other people think get in the way of not only her friendship with Charlie, but also showing everyone, including the bullies, who she is and what she has to say. title: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
shortSummary: We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and…
fullDescription: We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate the changing landscape. We will discuss current college admissions trends, admissions strategies, the changing test-optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find schools that can be a good fit, a timeline and other action steps to make this fall productive and help reduce the stress around the college admissions process. We'll examine the holistic admissions review process, what admissions officers consider important when they review applicants and how students can position themselves to develop a compelling narrative to increase their chances for admission. We will also discuss the importance of community service, how it can provide an opportunity for meaningful experiences, personal growth and a way to showcase a student's character. Admissions officers place great emphasis on a student's character including how the student has given back and helped others. This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens and is a detailed and strategic overview of what students should focus on for a successful college admissions process and how to reduce the stress around it. The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC. ( www.standoutforcollege.com ) Check the library page for registration, tickets, and any schedule updates.

title: Color Him Father
shortSummary: September is "Color Him Father" Month The New York Fathering Conference Committee, the White Plains Youth Bureau, Grandpas United, and JumpStart for Dads are…
fullDescription: September is "Color Him Father" Month The New York Fathering Conference Committee, the White Plains Youth Bureau, Grandpas United, and JumpStart for Dads are proud to designate the month of September as "Color Him Father" Month—a month-long celebration recognizing the invaluable role fathers, stepfathers, grandfathers, mentors, and father figures play in the lives of children and families. The theme, Color Him Father, is inspired by the classic R&B hit by The Winstons. The song tells the touching story of a stepfather who marries a widow and lovingly raises her children after their biological father is killed in the war. In appreciation of his love, sacrifice, guidance, and unwavering commitment, the children proudly proclaim, "Color Him Father." The song remains a timeless tribute to the profound impact a caring father figure can have on a child's life. Color Him Father Month is more than a celebration—it is a call to recognize, honor, and encourage fathers and father figures whose love, leadership, and presence help shape strong children, healthy families, and thriving communities. Through storytelling, education, and community engagement, these events will highlight the lasting impact that fathers have on future generations. Throughout September, a series of events will celebrate and elevate the importance of engaged fatherhood. Contact the Youth Bureau at 914-422-1378 for more information on these and all their events. Students and recent alumni from great music conservatories, including Juilliard, Bard, Yale, CUNY Graduate Center, SUNY Purchase and the Aaron Copland School of Music, participate in our concerts and receive stipends for their performances. Concerts take place in New Rochelle, Scarsdale, White Plains and Yonkers, bringing live music performances to community residents who might not be able to attend and enjoy these events. Please see more about our organization at https://www.youngmusiciansofwestchester.org/ Check the library page for registration, tickets, and any schedule updates.
